title: Extra Clicks at the Gate
statement: A counter at a gate starts at $0$. People pass through the gate one at a time. Each person adds $1$ to the counter, except that every sixth person (the $6$th, $12$th, $18$th and so on) adds $2$ instead. After the last person has passed through, the counter shows $500$. How many people passed through the gate?
hints: Work out what the first six people do to the counter altogether. Then do the same for the next six people.

Use block grouping: split the people into consecutive blocks of $6$. Every complete block contains exactly one person who adds $2$, so each block adds the same amount, $7$, to the counter. Now divide $500$ by $7$ to see how many complete blocks fit.

Since $500 = 71 \cdot 7 + 3$, the counter shows $497$ after $71$ complete blocks of $6$ people. The people in the next block each add $1$, until that block's sixth person. Work out how many more people are needed to add the remaining $3$, then include them in the total number of people.
solution: Split the people, in order, into consecutive blocks of $6$: persons $1$ to $6$, then persons $7$ to $12$, and so on. In each complete block, the first five people add $1$ each and the sixth adds $2$, so the block adds $5 + 2 = 7$ to the counter. Now divide $500$ by $7$ to get $500 = 71 \cdot 7 + 3$. After $71$ complete blocks, $71 \cdot 6 = 426$ people have passed through and the counter shows $71 \cdot 7 = 497$. The counter still has to rise by $3$. The next three people are persons $427$, $428$ and $429$. They are the first three people of a new block, so none of them is a multiple of $6$ in the count, and each adds exactly $1$. The counter therefore shows $498$, $499$ and then $500$. Every person raises the counter, so it never returns to $500$ later and it can show $500$ after only this one number of people. The number of people who passed through the gate is $426 + 3 = 429$. Why this works. block-grouping-of-sums, periodicity: the pattern of additions repeats every six people, so whole blocks each add $7$ and only a short remainder has to be counted by hand.
